html:
Jerash, ancient Gerasa, is a city north of Amman with some of the best preserved Roman ruins anywhere. It was one of the Decapolis, a group of Greek-speaking cities, and joined the Roman Empire in 63 BCE.

It grew rich in the 1st and 2nd centuries CE on farming and the caravan trade with the Nabataeans of Petra. Its long colonnaded street, oval plaza, theatres and temples date from that time, and an arch was built for the visit of the emperor Hadrian in 129. Later it had many churches.

An earthquake in 749 ruined much of the city, which then emptied. Sand covered and preserved it. The Jerash festival of music and theatre has been held in its ruins since 1981. See also Jordan.
sum: Jerash, ancient Gerasa, is a city north of Amman with some of the best preserved Roman ruins anywhere. It was one of the Decapolis, a group of Greek-speaking cities, and joined the Roman Empire in 63 BCE.
